newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to urge U.S. to drop ship sanctions threat.
newsitem.headline: Japan to urge U.S. to drop ship sanctions threat.

text.p: Japan will strongly request the United States to withdraw its threat to impose sanctions on Japanese ships in a dispute over practices at Japanese ports, Transport Minister Makoto Koga said in a statement on Thursday.

The statement was issued after the U.S. Maritime Commission announced on Wednesday that it would impose $100,000 port surcharges on Japanese vessels calling at U.S. ports. It said the surcharge would take effect on April 14.
"The Transport Ministry can in no way accept the U.S. decision and will strongly urge the commission to withdraw its decision," the statement said.
Japan will reserve the right to deal with the issue through multilateral and bilateral channels, it said.

Japan has repeatedly asked the United States not to take unilateral punitive measures as such action could violate World Trade Organisation rules and a Japan-U.S. shipping agreement, the statement said.
It said Japan would continue to make efforts to improve a "prior consultation" system of negotiations and pre-approvals involving carriers, a waterfront employees' association and waterfront unions.
Washington has said the association, or the Japan Harbour Transportation Association, has put in place costly and restrictive practices that discriminate against foreign vessels.
The U.S. Maritime Commission said shippers were not allowed to make operational changes, major or minor, without the permission of the association.
By refusing to license non-Japanese companies to perform stevedoring or terminal operating services, the Japanese government was discriminating against U.S. carriers, the commission said.
Repeated diplomatic efforts over the last several years by the United States and other trading partners had failed to bring about necessary reforms, it said.
